Inductive Exp Γ : Ty → Set := | EUnit : Exp Γ TyUnit | Pair {τ1 τ2} : Exp Γ τ1 → Exp Γ τ2 → Exp Γ (TyPair τ1 τ2) | Fst .. | Snd .. | VAR {τ} : Var Γ τ → Exp Γ τ | LAM {dom cod} : Exp (dom :: Γ) cod → Exp Γ (dom ⟶ cod) | APP {dom cod} : Exp Γ (dom ⟶ cod) → Exp Γ dom → Exp Γ cod. Inductive Obj : Set := One_ | Prod_ : Obj → Obj → Obj | Exp_ : Obj → Obj → Obj | Zero_ | Coprod_ : Obj → Obj → Obj.  -- file header: "this file builds the free such category on no generators as a term model"

Record OpSignature := { operation : Type ; arity : operation → Type }.  Record EqSignature (S : OpSignature) := { eq :> Type ; eq_arity : eq → Type ; lhs, rhs : ∀ (A : OpAlgebra S) (e : eq), (eq_arity e → A) → A ; lhs_natural ; rhs_natural }.  Record Algebra (S : OpSignature) (E : EqSignature S) := { alg :> OpAlgebra S ; equations : ∀ (e : E) args, lhs e args = rhs e args }.

(presentation by generators and equations, developed for PROPs: "presented by generators and relations is the free monoid quotiented ...") — the same recipe carried out one structural level down (symmetric strict monoidal), not for cartesian closed categories.

statement_record.book: A theory in the lambda-calculus is a set of basic types together with a set of basic terms (typed constants) and a set of equations between terms; for such a theory L the category of types C(L) is the cartesian closed category presented by those generators and relations.
statement_record.intree: Instance/Lambda/Ty.v: `Inductive Ty : Set := TyUnit | TyPair : Ty → Ty → Ty | TyArrow : Ty → Ty → Ty.` with header note "There are no extra base types: [TyUnit] is the only ground type"; Instance/Lambda/Exp.v: `Inductive Exp Γ : Ty → Set := EUnit | Pair | Fst | Snd | VAR | LAM | APP` (no constants); Instance/AST.v header: "the free such category on no generators".
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the in-tree lambda calculus is fixed at the EMPTY signature — one ground type, no typed constants, no axiom set — so a theory L (basic types + basic terms + equations) has no in-tree counterpart at all; only the trivial theory is realized. Signature+equations presentation machinery exists, but for first-order universal algebra with Sets-models only (Instance/Comp.v) and for PROPs (Construction/PROP/Presentation.v), never for the lambda-calculus/CCC pair. The `A : Type` / `L : HostExprsSem A` parameters of Instance/Lambda.v are explicitly documented as vestigial ("No class named [HostExprsSem] is in scope ... both are dropped"), i.e. the intended signature extension point exists only as a comment.

gap: No parameterization of the STLC by a signature: (i) no set of basic types (Ty is closed with TyUnit the sole ground type), (ii) no basic terms/typed constants (Exp has no constant constructor), (iii) no set of equations/axioms and no provable-equality judgement generated by them (Instance/Lambda/ carries only operational Step/multi reductions, and morphism equality in Lambda Γ is denotational agreement in the Coq model, not derivability). Consequently there is no `LambdaTheory` record and no `C(L)` parameterized by one — only C(empty theory).

Class ClosedFunctor := { fobj_exp_iso {x y : C} : F (y^x) ≅ F y ^ F x; exp_in := fun x y => from (@fobj_exp_iso x y); exp_out := fun x y => to (@fobj_exp_iso x y); fmap_curry {x y z} {f : x × y ~> z} : fmap (curry f) ≈ exp_in _ _ ∘ curry (fmap f ∘ prod_in); fmap_uncurry {x y z} (f : x ~> z^y) : fmap (uncurry f) ≈ uncurry (exp_out _ _ ∘ fmap f) ∘ prod_out }.  -- header: "Cartesian closed functors are exactly the morphisms of models of the simply-typed lambda calculus."

Fixpoint SemTy (τ : Ty) : Type := match τ with TyUnit => unit | TyPair t1 t2 => SemTy t1 * SemTy t2 | TyArrow dom cod => SemTy dom → SemTy cod end.  Fixpoint SemExp `(e : Exp Γ τ) : SemEnv Γ → SemTy τ (line 116) — 'the interpreting CCC is taken to be Coq's own universe [Type]'.

Record Model := { model_fun : @law_cat T ⟶ C; model_cartesian : @CartesianFunctor (@law_cat T) C model_fun (@law_cartesian T) _; model_terminal : @TerminalFunctor (@law_cat T) C model_fun (@law_terminal T) _ }.  (models of a LAWVERE — finite-product, first-order — theory in a cartesian C)

statement_record.book: A model of a lambda-theory L in a cartesian closed category C assigns an object [[X]] to each basic type X and an arrow [[b]] : [[A]] → [[B]] to each basic term b, extends structurally so that products/pairing/projections go to the categorical product, application to evaluation and abstraction to transposition, and satisfies every equation of L: if L ⊢ a = b then [[a]] = [[b]] (eq. 6.6).
statement_record.intree: Instance/AST.v `denote`/`interp`: a structural interpretation of the syntax of types into the object formers (1, ×, ^, 0, +) and of the syntax of arrows into id/∘/one/exl/exr/fork/curry/uncurry/zero/inl/inr/merge of an ARBITRARY bicartesian closed C. Functor/Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v `ClosedFunctor` is the CCC-structure-preserving functor (the functorial form of the same data).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the structural-extension clause of the book's definition is present in full (`denote`/`interp` carry every type former and every term former to the corresponding CCC structure, into an arbitrary C), but the two clauses that make it a model OF A THEORY are missing — there are no basic types/basic terms to assign values to (the signature is empty, see awodey:6.5:def-lambda-theory), and there is no equation-satisfaction requirement (eq. 6.6), because there is no set of equations and no derivability judgement. In Instance/Lambda/Sem.v the target CCC is additionally pinned to Coq's `Type` rather than being arbitrary. Theory/Lawvere/Model.v gives the honest 'model of a theory' pattern but for FIRST-ORDER (finite-product) theories: no exponentials, no higher types.

gap: Missing: a model record parameterized by a theory — i.e. (a) a valuation of basic types as objects and basic terms as arrows, and (b) the soundness requirement that the interpretation identify the arrows named by the theory's equations. In-tree there is only the interpretation of the empty theory (`interp` into any BiCCC) and the fixed Coq-model interpretation (`SemExp`). Also missing: the packaging of an interpretation as a CCC-preserving functor — `interp` is a Program Fixpoint with `interp_proper`, never shown to be a `Functor` carrying `CartesianFunctor`/`ClosedFunctor` witnesses.

evidence.intree_statement: Class MonoidObject (mon : C) := { mempty : I ~> mon; mappend : mon ⨂ mon ~> mon; mempty_left : mappend ∘ bimap mempty id ≈ to (@unit_left C _ mon); mempty_right : mappend ∘ bimap id mempty ≈ to (@unit_right C _ mon); mappend_assoc : mappend ∘ bimap mappend id ≈ mappend ∘ bimap id mappend ∘ to tensor_assoc }.

Definition Monoid := @MonoidObject C CC_Monoidal.  (* monoid object for the cartesian monoidal structure: tensor = ×, unit = terminal 1 — so mempty : 1 ~> mon and mappend : mon × mon ~> mon, exactly Awodey's [[u]] : 1 → M and [[m]] : M × M → M *)

#[export] Program Instance Hom_Monoid {x} `(Y : Monoid y) : @MonoidObject C CC_Monoidal (y ^ x) := { mempty := curry (@mempty _ _ _ Y ∘ exl); mappend := curry (@mappend _ _ _ Y ∘ uncurry exl △ uncurry exr) }.  (monoid objects in a CCC are closed under exponentials)

Program Definition Mon : Category := {| obj := { x : C & Monoid x }; hom := fun X Y => { f : `1 X ~> `1 Y & MonoidHom `2 X `2 Y f }; homset := fun _ _ => {| equiv := fun f g => `1 f ≈ `1 g |}; id := fun X => (id; MonoidHom_id `2 X); compose := fun _ _ _ f g => (`1 f ∘ `1 g; MonoidHom_comp `2 f `2 g) |}.
the analogous 'models of a theory = the classical algebraic structure' theorem proved in-tree for OPERADS: algebras of the terminal operad in Sets are commutative monoids, both directions.

statement_record.book: Let L be the lambda-theory with one basic type X and basic terms u : X, m : X × X → X subject to m<u,x> = x, m<x,u> = x, m<x,m<y,z>> = m<m<x,y>,z>. Then a model of L in a cartesian closed category C is precisely a monoid object in C: an object M with 1 → M and M × M → M satisfying unit and associativity.
statement_record.intree: Structure/Monoid.v: `Definition Monoid := @MonoidObject C CC_Monoidal.` where `Class MonoidObject (mon : C) := { mempty : I ~> mon; mappend : mon ⨂ mon ~> mon; mempty_left; mempty_right; mappend_assoc }` — instantiated at the cartesian monoidal structure this is exactly (M, 1 → M, M × M → M) with the unit and associativity laws.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the RIGHT-HAND side of the example — the monoid object in a (cartesian closed) category — is present in full, with the cartesian specialization `Monoid`, closure under products (`Product_Monoid`) and exponentials (`Hom_Monoid`), and a category `Mon C` of internal monoids with a faithful forgetful functor. The LEFT-hand side — the lambda-theory L presenting it — and the identification 'models of L in C = monoid objects in C' are entirely absent, since the library has no lambda-theories (see awodey:6.5:def-lambda-theory). Instance/Comp.v carries a signature+equations example, but it is the theory of GROUPS in universal-algebra form with Sets-models only, not the monoid lambda-theory with models in an arbitrary CCC.

evidence.intree_statement: #[export] Program Instance exp_prod_r {x y z : C} : (y × z)^x ≅ y^x × z^x := { to := curry (exl ∘ eval) △ curry (exr ∘ eval); from := curry (uncurry exl △ uncurry exr) }.  (both iso obligations discharged; Qed)

#[export] Program Instance exp_prod_l {x y z : C} : z^(x × y) ≅ (z^y)^x := { to := curry (curry (eval ∘ to prod_assoc)); from := curry (uncurry eval ∘ from prod_assoc) }.  (both iso obligations discharged; Qed)
Goal ∀ x y z : C,    (x × y)^z ≅ x^z × y^z.              auto. Qed.
Goal ∀ x y z : C,    x^(y × z) ≅ (x^y)^z.                auto. Qed.

#[export] Program Instance exp_swap {x y z : C} : (z^y)^x ≅ (z^x)^y := { to := to exp_prod_l ∘ to (@exp_respects_iso x y z _ _ (@prod_comm _ _ x y) z z iso_id) ∘ from exp_prod_l; ... }  (the symmetry corollary of part (b))

statement_record.book: For any three objects A, B, C of a cartesian closed category there are isomorphisms (a) (A × B)^C ≅ A^C × B^C and (b) (A^B)^C ≅ A^(B × C).
